newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- up slightly in light action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- up slightly in light action.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices gained about 1/8 point at midday Tuesday, amid a light new issue calendar and quiet activity.

One trader said the morning's housing starts figure, which came in as expected at 1.447 million, helped give the market a firm tone. With little else to focus on, that's been enough to keep prices higher at midday, the trader said.
Another tone setter could come at 1400 EDT, when bids are due on a sizeable bid-wanted list which one trader said would offer a better peg on where the market is heading.
Analysts said Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee would likely be a non-event, with no change in interest rates.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was higher, gaining 4/32 at 98-7/32 to yield 6.51 percent.

In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 8/32 at 120-13/32. The September T-bond contract was up 5/32 at 114-8/32, widening the MOB spread to 197 ticks from 194 at the close on Monday.
As for Tuesday's new muni issues, offerings are expected to total $474 million in 31 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
John Nuveen & Co tentatively priced the largest negotiated offering, a $79.5 million Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs revenue bond deal which carried a 5.80 percent yield in 2029.
On the competitive side, 19 sales totaling $239 million are scheduled. A $62 million Fort Bend Independent School District, Texas, offering was the largest, at 1300 EDT.
Smith Barney Inc won a $47 million Cherokee School District No 1, S.C., competitive deal, and reoffered the 2017 maturity at 5.30 percent.
In other new issue news, Florida Board of Education said it would sell $250 million bonds in a competitive sale Wednesday at 1100 EDT.

In the secondary market, bids on Dade County, Fla., FGIC 5-1/4s of 2026 were down two basis points to 5.45 percent. Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority 5.0s of 2024 were unchanged at 5.47 percent.
